solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fresh openings for a number of traditional singers

parts.note: fresh as in new and unripe, green
sleeves are the openings a garment has for the arms

explanation.surface: It reads like advice on giving folk singers some new opportunities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' is a musical number, a song, not a count of singers; 'for' just links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Greensleeves is an old English folk tune, a song long sung by traditional performers.

clue.text: Uproar about a fashionable black emblem used for the NHS

indicators.note: about means going round, so the uproar word wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: a row is a noisy quarrel or uproar
in means fashionable, as in 'the in thing'
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A fuss about a trendy dark logo chosen for Britain's health service.
explanation.walkthrough: The NHS is Britain's National Health Service; during the 2020 pandemic people put rainbows in windows to thank its staff.
explanation.definitionFit: The rainbow became a symbol of gratitude and support for health workers in Britain during lockdown.

clue.text: Tending to produce current clever item too freely

indicators.note: freely suggests the letters move about without constraint, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is criticised for being too clever with an item, used too liberally.
explanation.definitionFit: An electromotive force is what drives an electric current through a circuit.

clue.text: Run steamship around Great Lake

indicators.note: around means the steamship letters surround the lake

parts.note: Erie is one of North America's Great Lakes

explanation.surface: An instruction to sail a steamer around one of the Great Lakes.
explanation.definitionFit: A run of games or performances is a sequence, the same thing as a set of consecutive events.

clue.text: I concealed pay when working for a good reference

indicators.note: working suggests the letters are being put to work in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone admits hiding their salary while employed, in exchange for a good job reference.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A good reference' suggests a testimonial from an employer; here it is a reference book.
explanation.definitionFit: An encyclopaedia is a comprehensive reference work consulted for facts on many subjects.

clue.text: Four in six days will be bright

indicators.note: in places the four numeral inside the six numeral

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
IV is four in Roman numerals
D is the abbreviation for days, as in d for day

explanation.surface: A weather forecast: four sunny days in the next six.
explanation.definitionFit: Vivid colours are intense and brilliant, so the word is a synonym of bright.

clue.text: Bizarre marine mammal eating meat in hurry

indicators.note: eating means the mammal takes the other letters inside itself

parts.note: a seal is a marine mammal

indicators.note: the meat of a word is its inside, everything but the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A strange picture of a seal wolfing down meat in a rush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Meat' is not food here: the meat of a word is its inside, all but the outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Surreal means dreamlike and strange, a synonym for bizarre.

clue.text: Outback hospital is after transport for many passengers

indicators.note: is after places the hospital letter following the vehicle

parts.note: a bus carries many passengers
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A remote hospital is reachable only after a long bus ride.
explanation.definitionFit: The bush is the Australian term for the remote wild country, as is the outback.

clue.text: Join retinue returning after shelling

indicators.note: returning means the letters are read going back the other way
shelling strips the outer layer, so the first and last letters of retinue go

explanation.surface: A recruit joins an entourage coming home after a bombardment.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the outer letters of RETINUE to leave ETINU, then 'returning' turns it around.
explanation.definitionFit: To unite is to bring together into one, a synonym of join.

clue.text: Get back with protection by Royal Engineers

indicators.note: by means next to, so the two pieces sit side by side

parts.note: RE is the abbreviation for the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
cover is shelter or protection

explanation.surface: Soldiers retrieve something under the cover of army engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: To recover something is to regain possession of it, i.e. to retrieve it.

clue.text: Visitor frequently wants a short time in shade

indicators.note: in places the short-time pieces inside the shade word

parts.note: a hue is a shade of colour
a bit is a short while, as in 'wait a bit'

explanation.surface: A regular guest likes spending a little while in the shade.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitué is a regular, someone who often goes to a particular place.

clue.text: Scrounge penny once in prison

indicators.note: in puts the old penny letter inside the prison word

parts.note: a cage is a place of confinement
d was the abbreviation for a penny in pre-decimal British money

explanation.surface: A prisoner begs for a penny, as they once did.
explanation.definitionFit: To cadge is to beg or sponge something from another person, i.e. to scrounge.

clue.text: Knock out with weight — ouch! Fall on the floor?

parts.note: KO is the boxing abbreviation for knockout
ow is an exclamation of pain, like ouch

explanation.surface: A boxer flattened by a heavy blow cries out and hits the canvas.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits a loose definition: to kowtow is to kneel and touch the ground with the forehead.
explanation.definitionFit: Kowtowing is the old Chinese gesture of prostrating oneself on the ground in deference.

clue.text: Where one might see utensils and cold chicken?

definitions.text: Where one might see utensils and cold chicken?

parts.note: kit is a set of equipment or tools
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
a hen is a chicken

explanation.surface: A question about where you'd find pans and leftover chicken.
explanation.definitionFit: The room for cooking is where utensils are kept and cold meat is stored.

clue.text: Force company representative to take European line

parts.note: an MP, Member of Parliament, is an elected representative

explanation.surface: A firm's rep is pressured into taking the European line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take' is just a link: the pieces sit in order.
explanation.definitionFit: To compel someone is to oblige them by pressure, the verb sense of force.

clue.text: Hidden danger of wrong sort of fat in tablet

indicators.note: in puts the rearranged letters inside the tablet word

parts.note: a pill is a tablet of medicine

indicators.note: wrong sort of means the letters come out in a wrong order

explanation.surface: A diet pill containing a bad kind of fat is a health hazard.
explanation.definitionFit: A pitfall is an unsuspected trap or snag, literally a concealed pit.

clue.text: Plan scenic home movie on vacation

indicators.note: vacation is emptying out, so each word loses its inside and keeps only first and last letters

explanation.surface: A holiday plan: a scenic home video shot while away.
explanation.definitionFit: A scheme is a systematic plan of action, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Prohibited a bishop entering as well

indicators.note: entering means these pieces go into the as-well word

parts.note: too means as well, also
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop is banned from entering too.
explanation.definitionFit: Something taboo is forbidden by custom, which matches prohibited as an adjective.

clue.text: Prohibit working peer

parts.note: to bar is to prohibit or ban
on means working or functioning, as with a switched-on machine

explanation.surface: An order banning a member of the Lords from working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peer' looks like a verb meaning look closely; it is a noun, a member of the nobility.
explanation.definitionFit: A baron is the lowest rank of the British peerage, so a nobleman.

clue.text: Caught one making bowlers talk a lot

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a hatter makes hats, including bowler hats

explanation.surface: A cricket fielder holds a catch and the bowlers start gabbing.
explanation.walkthrough: Bowlers here are hats, not cricketers; a bowler hat is a hard round felt hat.
explanation.definitionFit: To chatter is to talk rapidly and incessantly about trivial things.

clue.text: Primarily, rip on purpose?

indicators.note: on means placed on top of, so in a down answer the letter sits above
primarily means first of all, so take the opening letter of rip

parts.note: an end is an aim or purpose

explanation.surface: A question whether something was torn deliberately.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and the definition: tearing apart on purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: To rend is to tear something violently apart, a deliberate ripping.

clue.text: Brave woman taking two drugs together

indicators.note: together means the two drug words are joined side by side

parts.note: 'two drugs' names a pair of drugs; the first is heroin
the second of the two drugs is E, slang for ecstasy

explanation.surface: A daring woman is taking two narcotics at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two drugs' names a pair: HEROIN followed by E, the slang letter for ecstasy.
explanation.definitionFit: A heroine is a woman admired for courage, the female equivalent of a hero.

clue.text: Reclaim sodden land of delta before wet weather

indicators.note: before places the delta letter ahead of the weather word

parts.note: D is delta in the NATO phonetic alphabet
rain is wet weather

explanation.surface: Farmers reclaim marshy delta land ahead of the rainy season.
explanation.definitionFit: To drain marshland is to remove its water so it can be used, reclaiming it.

clue.text: NE brown ale drunk in northeast is gone once it's consumed

indicators.note: in puts the rearranged letters inside the northeast abbreviation

parts.note: NE is the compass abbreviation for northeast

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters are tipsy and stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: Newcastle Brown Ale drunk in the North East disappears once it's consumed.
explanation.walkthrough: Newcastle Brown Ale is a beer from north-east England, which the surface evokes.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-renewable resource, like coal or oil, cannot be replaced once it is used up.
